questions.question: Draw up a table comparing the sole trader, partnership, private company and public company under: number of owners, legal personality, liability, capital, management, continuity and formation.
questions.expected_answer: Owners: 1; 2 or more; 1 or more shareholders; usually many shareholders. Legal personality: no; no; yes; yes. Liability: unlimited; unlimited (joint and several); limited; limited. Capital: owner's savings/loans (least); partners' contributions; shareholders, not public; public share issues, JSE (most). Management: owner; partners; directors (min 1); board (min 3) with professional managers. Continuity: no; no (ends when a partner leaves/dies/joins); yes; yes. Formation: easy, cheap; easy, agreement advised; register with CIPC, MOI; most complex, prospectus/listing.

questions.question: Describe the overall pattern of change as a business moves from sole trader to public company.
questions.expected_answer: It gains limited liability, legal personality, continuity and access to larger capital, and can employ professional managers; but it loses simplicity, privacy and the owner's direct control, while formation costs, legal requirements, audit and disclosure obligations increase.

questions.question: A family furniture factory with large debts wants to protect its members' homes, pass the business to the next generation and keep ownership in the family. Recommend a form of ownership and justify it.
questions.expected_answer: Private company ((Pty) Ltd). Limited liability: shareholders lose only their investment, protecting their homes from the company's debts. Legal personality and continuity: the company continues when founders retire or die and shares pass to children. Control: the MOI restricts transfer of shares and it cannot offer shares to the public, so ownership stays in the family. Not a sole trader/partnership (unlimited liability, no continuity) nor a public company (unnecessary cost, disclosure, loss of control).
